transcript.text: Beko vented dryer, drum goes round fine but it's just blowing cold air. Had it about 6 years. What part do I need?

I can’t say which part you need yet because I don’t know if it’s a simple blockage or a failed heater, and buying parts blind is risky. On a Beko vented dryer like yours, cold air while the drum turns is often caused by a tripped thermal cut-out due to restricted airflow, but it could also be a failed heating element, thermostat, or just the wrong programme setting. Please check these two things first: clean the fluff filter in the door opening and ensure the vent hose at the back isn’t kinked or blocked. Then run a standard heat programme for 10–15 minutes with the power on to see if it starts warming up.

Done both. Filter was fairly full so I cleaned it, and the vent hose had a sag full of fluff which I cleared out. Airflow at the hose end seems decent now, but it's still cold after 20 min on a heat programme. Also it's the same on high and low heat. The vent was heavily clogged before it failed, and the last few weeks it had been taking longer to dry. What part do I need?

I can't tell you which part to buy yet because we haven't confirmed if the heating element is actually dead or just tripped by heat. Since cleaning the filter and clearing the vent didn't fix it, the thermal cut-out may have blown due to that previous blockage, or the heater itself has failed. To find the correct replacement part for your specific Beko model, I need the exact model number from you. This is usually on a sticker inside the door opening; if the door won't open right now, we can wait until it does.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

Front says DV7110 but I can't read the full model or serial, the label's on the back and it's wedged against the wall in a tight alcove. Can you work it out from DV7110? I've no multimeter either so can't do continuity tests.

Since you've already cleaned the filter and vent but it's still blowing cold air after 20 minutes, we can rule out simple blockages. The most common cause now is a failed heating element or a tripped thermal cut-out that won't reset. You'll need to pull the machine forward safely (switched off first) so you can read the full label on the back to find the right parts.
